The request is sent once for every tab the action runs on. Only a 2xx answer counts as success; redirects are not followed and count as failures. Cookies are not sent. Values are URL encoded in the URL and in a form body, and escaped in a JSON or XML body.
Tap an example to fill in the fields above. Then put your own server in place of example.com, and your own keys and IDs in place of the parts in capitals.

Dejavu has no ads. If you enjoy it, a coffee helps it grow.

Firefox Sync only shares the open tabs of each device. Tabs you open or close here also open or close on that device, but you can’t pin tabs, add folders or essentials, or choose a container. The name and icon come from the device, and the colors you pick stay on this phone.
Firefox Sync doesn’t share workspaces, so this workspace, with its pinned tabs and folders, stays on this phone. Firefox shows its open tabs as this phone’s tabs.
Tabs you are not using sleep to free memory

A sleeping tab frees its memory and loads its page again when you open it. The tab you are looking at, the one next to it in split view and tabs playing sound or using the camera or microphone stay awake. When Android needs memory while Dejavu is in the background, every tab but the two you used last goes to sleep.

Changing these settings can weaken Dejavu\'s security and privacy, or break websites. If you change one behind Dejavu\'s tracking protection, it is managed here until you reset it. Others that Dejavu\'s settings control go back to them when Dejavu restarts.

While it is on, a computer connected to this phone over USB, with USB debugging allowed, can control Dejavu and read its data, like open tabs, cookies and saved passwords, without asking. Turn it off when you are done.
The people you call and the sites that make calls can then see your IP address. Sites you let use your camera or microphone can also see your addresses on your local network.
On phones with Google Play Services, Android finds your location by sending the Wi-Fi networks and cell towers near you to Google. Websites still get your location only after you allow them.
This build of Dejavu has no Safe Browsing key, so it cannot warn about dangerous sites.
Trackers, fingerprinting, secure connections and more
A protection that is on keeps you safer. Each one says what it guards against and what may stop working because of it.
You changed this in about:config, so it is managed there. Reset it in about:config to change it here.
Pages open only over secure connections, which no one on your network can read or change. Dejavu asks before opening a page that has no secure version.
Private tabs open pages only over secure connections. In other tabs, someone on your network could read or change pages that are not secure.
Turn on so pages open only over secure connections, which no one on your network can read or change.
Dejavu looks up sites through %1$s over an encrypted connection, so your network and internet provider cannot see which sites you visit.
Turn on so your network and internet provider cannot see which sites you visit.
If %1$s cannot be reached, Dejavu warns you before it uses your network\'s DNS, which can see the sites you visit.
Turn on so Dejavu warns you before it falls back to your network\'s DNS, which can see the sites you visit.
Some pages may miss parts, like embedded videos or comments, but the ads and trackers in them cannot follow you.
Only private tabs block ads, videos and other content that track you.
Turn on so ads, videos and other content that track you do not load.
Sign-ins and payments that go through another site may not work, but no site can use cookies to follow you to other sites.
Each site already keeps its cookies to itself. Turn on to block cookies from other sites entirely.
Sites cannot secretly use your phone to mine cryptocurrency and drain its battery. Nothing stops working.
Turn on so sites cannot secretly use your phone to mine cryptocurrency and drain its battery.
Companies known for it cannot recognize your phone from its settings. Nothing stops working.
Turn on so companies known for it cannot recognize your phone from its settings.
Pages see less about your phone, like its screen and fonts, so they cannot recognize it. A few sites, like drawing or map tools, may act oddly.
Private tabs show pages less about your phone, like its screen and fonts. Other tabs show more, so every site works.
Turn on so pages see less about your phone, like its screen and fonts, and cannot recognize it.
Dejavu deletes the cookies of trackers that links send you through on the way to a site. Nothing stops working.
Turn on to delete the cookies of trackers that links send you through on the way to a site.
The tracking parts that sites add to links, like fbclid, are removed before the page opens. Nothing stops working.
Turn on to remove the tracking parts that sites add to links, like fbclid, before the page opens.
Sites are told not to sell or share your data, and the law makes some of them listen. Nothing stops working.
Turn on to tell sites not to sell or share your data.
Dejavu lets through the few trackers that sites need to work, so sites do not break.
Dejavu lets through only the trackers that sites cannot work without. Some sites may lose small things, like a video.
Every tracker is blocked, even the ones sites need to work, so some sites may break.
Sites where you turned tracking protection off.
Dejavu warns you before sites that spread malware or steal passwords. To check them, it sends Google short, scrambled pieces of some addresses.
Turn on to be warned before sites that spread malware or steal passwords. Dejavu then checks addresses with Google.
Sites run slower, but many attacks on browsers stop working. Takes full effect after Dejavu restarts.
Turn on to stop many attacks on browsers. Sites would run slower.
3D maps, games and some sites do not work, but sites cannot use your graphics chip to attack or recognize your phone.
Turn on so sites cannot use your graphics chip to attack or recognize your phone. 3D maps and games would stop working.
Calls on some sites may not connect, but sites and the people you call cannot see your IP address.
Turn on so sites and the people you call cannot see your IP address.
Finding your location may be slow or fail indoors, but Google does not learn where you are from the Wi-Fi networks around you.
Turn on so sites get your location from GPS only, without Google learning about the Wi-Fi networks around you.
Off. Dejavu collects no usage data and sends no crash reports.
Choose for each site what it may use, like your camera or location.
